title: Trưng sisters
capsule: The Trưng sisters — Trưng Trắc and Trưng Nhị — were Lạc Việt aristocrats who launched a revolt against Han Chinese rule in 40 CE after the Chinese governor Su Ding executed Trưng Trắc's husband Thi Sách; within months they had liberated sixty-five towns and settlements from the Red River Delta south through Rinan, and Trưng Trắc was proclaimed queen regnant with her capital at Mê Linh. Emperor Guangwu dispatched general Ma Yuan with roughly 20,000 troops in 42 CE; by spring 43 CE the sisters were defeated, and while Chinese sources record their capture and beheading, Vietnamese tradition holds they drowned themselves in the Hát River rather than submit. They are venerated throughout Vietnam as national liberators, with annual February commemoration and temples dedicated to their memory.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Trưng sisters' revolt is attested in Han dynastic histories and later Vietnamese chronicles, but the territorial extent of their control — especially the 65 commanderies cited in some sources — is a traditional figure and the actual administrative reach of their authority remains uncertain.
